stem: A project requires an initial investment of 2,500 and is expected to generate after-tax cash flows of 900 at the end of each of the next four years. If the required rate of return is 12%, the project's NPV is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. 1,100 is the undiscounted surplus (4 × 900 - 2,500); it ignores the time value of money.
rationale.B: Correct. Discounting four payments of 900 at 12% gives 2,733.61, so NPV = 233.61.
rationale.C: Incorrect. -338.35 discounts only three cash flows of 900, omitting the fourth year.

verify: let pv=0; for(let t=1;t<=4;t++) pv+=900/1.12**t; return pv-2500;

stem: A firm with a 10% cost of capital must choose one of two mutually exclusive projects. Project X has an IRR of 22% and an NPV of 40. Project Y has an IRR of 16% and an NPV of 65. The firm should:
options: choose Project X, because it has the higher IRR
reject both, because the IRRs disagree
choose Project Y, because it has the higher NPV
explanation: When NPV and IRR rank mutually exclusive projects differently, NPV is the better guide because it measures the value added to shareholders in money terms and uses a realistic reinvestment assumption.

rationale.A: Incorrect. IRR ignores scale and assumes reinvestment at the IRR; a higher IRR does not mean more value created.
rationale.B: Incorrect. Both projects exceed the 10% hurdle and have positive NPVs; conflicting rankings do not mean both should be rejected.
rationale.C: Correct. Project Y adds 65 of value versus 40 for Project X, so it maximises shareholder wealth.

stem: When estimating the cash flows of a proposed new product line, an analyst should exclude:
options: the cost of a consumer survey on the product completed and paid for last year
lost after-tax profits on an existing product that the new line will partly replace
the rental income the firm forgoes by using its own vacant warehouse for the project
explanation: The survey is a sunk cost: it has been paid whatever the decision, so it is not incremental. Cannibalisation and forgone rent are relevant incremental effects.

rationale.A: Correct. Sunk costs cannot be recovered by rejecting the project and must be ignored.
rationale.B: Incorrect. Cannibalised sales are a negative externality that reduces incremental cash flow and must be included.
rationale.C: Incorrect. Forgone rent is an opportunity cost and must be charged to the project.

stem: A pharmaceutical company builds a small pilot plant with the right, but not the obligation, to add a full-scale facility if trials succeed. This feature is best described as:
explanation: The right to scale up if results are favourable is an expansion option, which adds value beyond the pilot plant's static NPV.

rationale.A: Incorrect. An abandonment option is the right to exit if results are poor, not to grow if they are good.
rationale.B: Correct. Adding capacity after success is the classic expansion option.
rationale.C: Incorrect. A timing option is the right to delay the initial investment; here the pilot is already being built.
